passages.provision_quote: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase
passages.note: Bill text page prints the statewide rent-cap provision; carries no actor or tally.
Assembly Floor concurrence vote, the final Assembly vote before chaptering; Robert Rivas voted Aye.

rows.reasoning: Robert Rivas voted Aye on AB 1482 (2019-2020), a single-subject tenancy bill, whose operative section caps annual rent increases statewide at '5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower' and adds statewide just-cause eviction protections, while exempting new construction, single-family/condo owners, and other narrow categories. This creates and extends tenant protections to units not previously covered, matching the rung text 'Strengthen existing rent stabilization and extend coverage to more units,' and it excludes rung 1 ('all rental units communitywide') because of the bill's substantial exemptions.
